content.title: Keyboard Access and Visible Focus
content.hook: Not every user operates a page with a mouse. Keyboard access is also useful when a pointing device is unavailable, difficult to use, or simply not preferred.
content.context: The basic test is simple: can you reach and operate the page’s important controls with the keyboard?
goals: Understand keyboard navigation, preserve visible focus, and identify why a mouse-only interface is incomplete.

content.question: You load a page and want to perform the main task without using the mouse. What should you try first?

options.text: Press Tab and observe where focus moves.

feedback.correct: Tab is a practical first check for moving focus through common interactive elements.
feedback.incorrect: Tab is a practical first check for moving focus through common interactive elements.

content.title: Focus is location
content.text: When the keyboard moves through controls, the user needs to know which control currently has focus. Removing the visible focus indicator can make the interface feel as if the keyboard is “doing nothing.”

activities.title: Do not erase focus without a replacement

content.title: Do not erase focus without a replacement

content.question: What is the main problem with the CSS above if it is used without providing another clear focus style?

options.text: Keyboard users may lose the visual signal showing which control has focus.

feedback.correct: A visible focus indication is important. If you replace the browser’s default focus style, replace it with a clear alternative rather than simply removing it.
feedback.incorrect: A visible focus indication is important. If you replace the browser’s default focus style, replace it with a clear alternative rather than simply removing it.

content.title: Tiny keyboard route
content.text: Try this sequence on a small page: Tab from the top, name each control as it receives focus, then activate the main action without using the mouse. If you cannot tell where you are, stop and investigate the focus state.

options.text: It only responds to a mouse click.
It can be reached and meaningfully operated through the keyboard.

feedback.correct: Keyboard accessibility concerns both reachability and operation, not appearance alone.
feedback.incorrect: Keyboard accessibility concerns both reachability and operation, not appearance alone.

content.title: Hints for the lab
content.text:
Hint 1: Start with Tab.

Hint 2: Look for a visible focus indicator.

Hint 3: Check whether every important control can be reached and activated without a mouse.
